where_qualloop_adds_value_over_c.area: False Pause Prevention via Shrinkage & Credible Intervals
where_qualloop_adds_value_over_c.evidence: Across all 140 good ads in holdout, Baseline C false-pauses 19 good ads (FPPR = 13.57% [8.87%, 20.21%]), whereas QualLoop false-pauses only 2 good ads (FPPR = 1.43% [0.39%, 5.06%]). QualLoop's empirical-Bayes shrinkage pulls noisy small-sample estimates toward the portfolio mean, and its 80% credible interval requires high statistical confidence before taking destructive pause actions.

In 'healthy_campaign' (all good ads), Baseline C pauses 11 good ads (FPPR = 36.67%) because early mature conversions accidentally fell below the 15% hurdle before stabilizing. QualLoop paused 0 good ads (FPPR = 0.00%), delivering 2,017.63 qualified leads vs Baseline C's 1,866.70.
In the fixed redistributed budget variant, QualLoop generates 4,805.88 total qualified leads vs Baseline C's 4,737.22 leads (+68.66 leads), achieving a lower overall CPQL (₹170.83 vs ₹173.31).

where_qualloop_does_not_add_value_over_c.evidence: In 'bad_ad_high_engagement', where lead volume is high (8 leads/day) and intent is unequivocally low (3%), contacts rapidly exceed 15+ within the first week. Here, Baseline C's simple point estimate correctly pauses the bad ad at Day 7, matching QualLoop. In such asymptotic data regimes, shrinkage has minimal effect.

where_qualloop_does_not_add_value_over_c.area: Multi-ad Portfolio Trade-offs Under Fixed Budget
where_qualloop_does_not_add_value_over_c.evidence: In 'mixed_portfolio', Baseline C terminates the bad ad slightly faster than QualLoop due to its hard point cutoff, reallocating spend to good ads earlier and achieving 501.39 qualified leads vs QualLoop's 450.42. QualLoop's conservative credible interval requires more mature contact proof before pausing, incurring a latency cost when an ad is truly poor but has marginal early counts.
